hook: A rock discovered in the Sahara Desert is 4.1 billion years old.

sections.voiceover: A rock discovered in the Sahara Desert is 4.1 billion years old.
sections.visual_cue: Macro shot of a dark, pitted meteorite specimen resting on golden desert sand.
b_roll: Sahara Desert sand dunes landscape shot

sections.voiceover: But what makes the Teghaza 001 meteorite, a rare rock from Mars, so incredibly special?
sections.visual_cue: Geological expedition graphics mapping the 8 recovered fragment locations across desert coordinates.
b_roll: Geologists examining rock specimens in field

sections.voiceover: This Martian rock from the Sahara Desert formed at least 4.1 billion years ago.
sections.visual_cue: Microscopic cross-section of meteorite minerals under polarized laser illumination.

sections.voiceover: Scientists publishing in Science determined the rock formed 4.1 billion years ago. Altogether, the 8 recovered fragments weigh exactly 798.5 grams.
sections.visual_cue: 3D visualization of ancient volcanic Mars transitioning to the Teghaza 001 fragment.

sections.voiceover: NASA scientists study this 4.1 billion year old igneous rock from the planet Mars.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom out from Teghaza 001 to a view of planet Mars in deep space.
b_roll: Full globe rendering of red planet Mars
